rationale: B wins because it is tougher about what cannot go out the door yet: "without it this angle is unpitchable" is the sentence a founder needs before they embarrass themselves. A has sharper packaging in "Klarna Won't Say How Many Customer-Service Jobs It Eliminated," but then blows past its own evidentiary caution with "the Equivalent of 700 People Are Gone." B has one speculative angle, but its proof gates and counsel warning make it more useful strategic material.
gaps_in_A: "But the Equivalent of 700 People Are Gone" overstates the record. The update says the assistant handled equivalent work, not that 700 people are gone.
"The Headcount It Cut Is the Margin It's Showing Investors" implies causation and margin mechanics the update does not prove.
"advocacy concerns surfacing now are likely to precede regulatory attention" decorates a supplied concern into a regulatory forecast.
Misses the IPO-window legal gate. Before pitching headcount, profitability, and resolution-time metrics, counsel clearance is not optional.
gaps_in_B: "The other third got harder" is a strong angle, but it is not established by the supplied facts. It needs to be framed as a question until residual-caseload data exists.
"the machine takes the two-thirds that were resolvable in minutes" assumes why those chats stayed with the assistant. The update only says two-thirds of chats are AI-handled.
"Klarna won't say how many jobs the AI cut" is dismissed as "not an angle you pitch," too absolute. Labor opacity tied to an IPO can be a real reporter-shaped story.
"support desk automated" slightly overclaims; the facts say two-thirds of customer-service chats, not the entire support desk.
